Consult Summary:
- 48-year-old male (conflict noted in DOB/age) with 3 days of diarrhoea, central abdominal pain, nausea and one episode of vomiting; clinician impression: likely gastroenteritis — advised fluids, symptomatic care, and GP review if not improving.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Three days of diarrhoea with increased frequency and urgency; needing to remain close to toilet.
  - Central/sub‑umbilical abdominal pain, described as mild to moderate; some audible bowel sounds and sensation of trapped gas.
  - Nausea with one episode of vomiting this morning (patient uncertain if any blood — likely ingested strawberry fragments).
- Timeline:
  - Symptoms began approximately 3 days ago and have neither clearly worsened nor improved per patient.
  - Vomiting occurred this morning.
  - Patient reports sweating over the last 4 days but is unsure if this represented fever.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Going to the toilet provides some transient relief.
  - Patient has been avoiding large meals; reports possibly inadequate oral fluid intake.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - No reported visible blood per rectum.
  - No chest pain.
  - No new or worsening breathing problems beyond baseline asthma.
  - Ambulates and speaks normally but limits walking because of frequent toilet need.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No definite fever documented.
  - No documented hematemesis (patient uncertain, likely food).
  - No additional systemic symptoms documented.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma — uses an inhaler (details not documented).
- No other chronic medical conditions mentioned.

Medications:
- Inhaler — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- No other medications documented.

Allergies:
- Patient stated "NKDA" (no known drug allergies).

Social History:
- Patient identifies as a foreign national (mentions being a "foreigner"); some language difficulty noted.
- Unable to attend work currently due to frequent toilet needs.
- Reports he may not be drinking enough fluids.
- No explicit smoking, alcohol, or substance use history documented.

Family History:
- Father died approximately 10 years ago of bowel cancer.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Abdominal exam: Mild tenderness on central abdominal palpation (patient reports pressing causes a little pain).
- Respiratory/other findings: No acute respiratory distress reported; walking and talking normal.
- No other examination findings documented.

Investigations:
- None documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute diarrhoea with central abdominal pain and vomiting — suspected gastroenteritis (infectious/food‑related)
  - Plan:
    - Advise increased oral fluid intake and rehydration.
    - Monitor for fever and systemic deterioration.
    - Stay home/rest until improvement.
    - Avoid antibiotics (clinician advised antibiotics typically not helpful and may worsen course).
    - If symptoms worsen or do not improve over next 24–48 hours, arrange face‑to‑face GP assessment for abdominal examination and further workup.
    - If severe deterioration (high fever, severe abdominal pain, inability to tolerate fluids, signs of dehydration, blood in stool or vomit), seek urgent care/emergency services.
- Issue 2: Asthma (chronic)
  - Assessment:
    - Baseline asthma reported; patient uses an inhaler and recently obtained a new inhaler brand.
    - No acute respiratory compromise documented during consult.
  - Plan:
    - No acute interventions documented.
    - Advise to monitor breathing; seek urgent review if increased breathlessness or other asthma exacerbation signs.
- Issue 3: Family history of bowel cancer (father deceased ~10 years ago)
  - Assessment:
    - Patient concerned about personal risk given family history.
    - Clinician considers current presentation less suggestive of familial bowel cancer given acute infectious picture.
  - Plan:
    - If diarrhoea and abdominal symptoms persist or recur, arrange GP review and consider appropriate investigations (to be determined by GP).
- General plan items:
  - Patient to wait a couple of days and book/attend GP if not improving.
  - Patient advised to return earlier if symptoms worsen.

Quality checks:
- Missing but expected elements:
  - Vital signs (temperature, pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation) not documented.
  - Specific inhaler name, dose, route and frequency not documented.
  - Detailed stool characteristics (volume, consistency) and exact frequency not quantified.
  - No medication reconciliation or current medication list beyond inhaler.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Patient initially stated date of birth 01/01/1992 then later stated age 48 — conflict noted between DOB and stated age.
  - Uncertain report of blood in vomit: patient initially thought there might be blood, then attributed appearance to strawberries — conflict/uncertainty noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Consultation audio/transcript intelligible with some pauses and repetition; occasional minor language difficulty but clinical information retrievable.
